cases.situation: My friend Tara sent me her wedding speech for her sister and asked for honest thoughts. The story about teaching her sister to ride a bike is lovely, but the speech runs 7 minutes and the middle is mostly camp stories full of inside jokes nobody else will get.
cases.reply: I read it twice, and the bit about teaching her to ride a bike is my favourite part; keep that exactly as it is. Where I got a bit lost was the middle, with the camp stories: I didn't know the references, and I think a lot of the room won't either. If you kept one of those and cut the rest, it'd be a lot shorter and the bike story would hit even harder. This is going to be lovely.
cases.note: Specific praise first, one main issue as her experience as a listener, one concrete fix, and the goal restated.

cases.situation: 好朋友阿杰自己设计了新房的装修方案，下周一开工，发给我问真实意见。厨房和收纳设计得很用心，但他把客厅四面墙都定成深灰色，那套房子朝北，我去看房那天白天都要开灯。
cases.reply: 阿杰，方案我仔细看了，厨房和收纳那块看得出你花了很多心思。我唯一有点担心的是客厅的深灰色：房子朝北，那天去看房白天都得开灯，我怕四面深灰刷上去会更暗。要不只刷一面深灰做背景墙，其他三面用浅一点的颜色？开工前改最省事，我是想让你住进去每天都觉得舒服。
cases.note: 开工前是改起来最便宜的时候：只提一个问题，用自己看房时的亲身感受来说，再给一个折中的办法。

cases.situation: My husband Tom has been learning guitar for a year and wants to play and sing a song at his mum's 70th in two weeks. He played it for me tonight and asked what I really think. The chord changes are solid now, but he speeds up as soon as he starts singing.
cases.reply: Honestly? Your chord changes are really solid now, they sound smooth and sure. The one thing I noticed is that once you start singing it speeds up, and by the last chorus I felt like you were racing to the end. Want to run it a few times this week with a metronome, or with me tapping the beat? I'm only saying it because your mum is going to love this, and I want you to walk off feeling great.
cases.note: With a partner, face to face: one fixable thing with time to fix it, and nothing about what he can't change in two weeks, like his voice.

cases.situation: My friend Ollie hosted his first dinner party on Saturday for eight of us and texted the next day asking how it really went, because he's hosting his in-laws next month. The lamb was excellent, but he spent most of the night alone in the kitchen and we didn't eat the main until after 10pm.
cases.reply: Honestly? The lamb was excellent, I'd happily eat it again tomorrow. The one thing I'd change for your in-laws is the timing: you spent most of the night in the kitchen, and by the time the main came out after 10 we'd missed having you at the table. What if you picked dishes you can make ahead, so you're sitting down with everyone when they arrive? I'm only saying it because the cooking is clearly there.
cases.note: When it's already over, aim the one point at the next time they mentioned, not at what can't be undone.

cases.situation: Mon ami Julien a organisé notre week-end à quatre à Lisbonne du 23 au 25 octobre et m'a demandé ce que je pensais vraiment du programme. Les restaurants qu'il a choisis ont l'air géniaux, mais chaque journée est remplie de 8 h à minuit, sans aucune pause.
cases.reply: Julien, merci d'avoir tout organisé, les restaurants que tu as choisis me font déjà envie. Ce qui m'inquiète un peu, c'est le rythme : de 8 h à minuit tous les jours, j'ai peur qu'on soit épuisés dès le samedi soir. Et si on gardait un après-midi libre chaque jour, sans rien de prévu ? Je te dis ça parce que je veux qu'on profite vraiment de tout ce que tu as trouvé.
cases.note: Quand le programme vous concerne aussi, parlez de ce que vous ressentez, pas de ses choix, et proposez un seul ajustement simple.

cases.situation: Hired a freelance designer, Amara, for our cafe logo. The first round of 3 concepts came in; the lettering on concept 2 is lovely, but all three feel corporate, and we're a tiny neighbourhood cafe with mismatched mugs and a chalkboard menu. Round two is included and I don't want to crush her.
cases.reply: Hi Amara, thanks for these. The lettering on concept 2 is lovely. Seeing all three together made me realise they feel more corporate than we are: we're a tiny neighbourhood cafe with mismatched mugs and a chalkboard menu, so I think the logo should feel hand-made and warm. Could round two push in that direction, maybe starting from the concept 2 lettering? Happy to do a 15-minute call if that's easier.
cases.note: With a paid creative, describe the direction you want, not just 'not quite it', and keep one real thing to build on.

cases.situation: 我爸退休后开始写回忆录，写完前三章发给我，说想听听真实意见。写他1978年进厂当学徒、师傅让他锉了一整天铁块那段写得很好，但大部分是按年份一件件记流水账，读着有点累。
cases.reply: 爸，前三章我认真看完了。写您1978年进厂当学徒那段特别好，师傅让您锉了一整天铁块，我读的时候好像都能听见那个声音。我读着有点吃力的是其他部分，一年一年往下记，事情一多，反而看不出哪些对您最重要。要不每章就挑一两件您印象最深的事，像锉铁块那样展开写？这本东西值得写好，我想一直留着。
cases.note: 对长辈也是一样：先说一处真实具体的好，再只提一个问题，用'我读着'描述感受，最后回到这件事的意义。

cases.situation: My friend Dani did her first open mic last week and asked what I thought. I told her the dentist opener killed but the middle bit about dating apps felt like stuff we've heard before. Now she's texting 'so you thought it was bad?? just tell me it was good'.
cases.reply: I don't think it was bad. The dentist bit was the best thing I heard all night. The middle isn't there yet, and I think it can be, which is the only reason I said it. If you want a cheerleader for the next one, just say and I'll be the loudest person in the room.
cases.note: When they push you to say it was good, hold the point without adding to it, and offer to be the cheerleader next time if that's what they want.

cases.situation: My 17-year-old son Eli asked me to read his college essay, due Nov 1. It's all about winning the state debate final and reads like a résumé. The one paragraph about his grandpa driving him to practice at 6am is the only part that sounds like him.
cases.reply: I read it twice. The paragraph about Grandpa driving you to practice at 6am is the best thing in it; that's the part that sounds like you. Where I lost the thread was the rest, which tells me what you won more than who you are, and I'd guess admissions readers see a lot of trophy essays. What if the whole essay grew out of those car rides? It's your essay and your call. I'm only saying it because I think there's a really good one in here.
cases.note: With your own teenager: one point, framed as a reader's experience, and the decision handed back. It's his essay, not yours.

cases.situation: 闺蜜小雨准备在相亲软件上重新写个人资料，发给我让我提真实意见。照片选得挺好，尤其是在大理骑车那张，但自我介绍全是“不要抽烟的”“不要妈宝男”这种，读下来像在设门槛。
cases.reply: 你问我真实意见，那我就直说啦。照片选得特别好，第二张在大理骑车那张，一看就是你。最可以改的是自我介绍：现在写的大多是“不要什么”，读下来有点像在设门槛。要不改成三件你真正喜欢做的事？我是觉得你这么有意思的人，资料应该让人一眼就看出来。
cases.note: 先说一个具体的优点，只挑最重要的一个问题，用“我读下来的感受”来讲，再给一个能直接改的建议。

cases.situation: My friend Nadia just launched her jewelry shop on Etsy and posted the link in our group chat. The pieces are lovely, especially the hammered silver hoops, but the photos are dark and shot on a busy floral tablecloth. She didn't ask for feedback.
cases.reply: Nadia, congrats on the launch! The hammered silver hoops are gorgeous, I'd wear them tomorrow. I've got one small thought about the photos if you want it, or I can just be your cheerleader today. Either is fine.
cases.note: Unasked means ask first, and in a private message, not the group; if she says yes, give only the one point: daylight and a plain background.

cases.situation: My friend Dev, 38, hasn't exercised in years and has signed up for a marathon on Sunday 22 November. He sent me his training plan and asked for my honest take: it has rest days and a food plan, but it jumps straight to 30-mile weeks, and last month he told me his knee has been aching.
cases.reply: I love that you've actually written a plan, and the rest days and food plan are more than most people bother with. The one thing that worries me is going straight to 30-mile weeks from no running at all, especially with your knee aching last month. Would you see a doctor or a physio about the knee before you start, and ask them how fast to build up? I'm saying this because I want you on that start line, not on the sidelines with an injury.
cases.note: When the plan carries a health risk, the one point is the risk, and the suggestion is a check with a professional, not your own training advice.

cases.situation: My friend Priya shot our small wedding for free as her gift and sent 30 preview photos, asking what we think before she edits the other 400. The shot of my dad during the vows made me cry, but she's used a heavy orange filter on all but a few church shots and our skin looks very tanned. We're so grateful and don't want to hurt her.
cases.reply: Priya, thank you for these. The shot of Dad during the vows made me cry. One small request for the rest: could they be a bit more natural in colour? We both look a little orange next to how we remember the day. The few church shots without the filter are exactly right. Thank you, truly, for this gift.
cases.note: Because it's a gift and she asked before editing the rest, one specific, fixable request with a clear example is kind, not ungrateful.

cases.situation: 8岁的女儿朵朵写了一篇作文《我的妈妈》，下周交给学校参加比赛，拿来问我写得怎么样。写我下雨天去接她、伞全往她那边歪那一段特别真，但后面一大段是“我的妈妈很漂亮，很勤劳，很善良”这样的套话。
cases.reply: 朵朵，妈妈认真看完了。写下雨天我去接你、伞全往你那边歪那一段，妈妈特别喜欢，那是只有你才写得出来的。后面说妈妈很漂亮、很勤劳那几句，读起来跟别的小朋友写的有点像。要不要把它们换成另一件你记得的小事，像下雨天那样写？你已经会写最难的那种句子了，再改一点点就更好了。
cases.note: 对小孩也只提一个点：先夸具体的那段，再用“像这样再写一件”给出她能照着做的办法。

cases.situation: My partner Mei finished the first draft of a short story at 1am and sent it to me with just 'thoughts?'. The opening line about her grandmother's sewing tin is perfect, but the ending feels rushed. She's often hard on herself late at night.
cases.reply: That opening line about your grandmother's sewing tin is perfect, I keep thinking about it. Before I say more: do you want a cheerleader tonight or an editor tomorrow? Either is completely fine, and I've got thoughts ready whenever you want them.
cases.note: When 'thoughts?' could mean either and it's late, give one real compliment and ask what kind of feedback she wants before giving the critique.

cases.situation: 好朋友阿琳开了家咖啡店，这周试营业，特意请我去喝，让我提真实意见。手冲和肉桂卷都很好，但菜单上有二十多种饮品，我点单时纠结了半天，后面排队的人也等得不耐烦。
cases.reply: 阿琳，先说好的：你的手冲是我今年喝过最干净的，肉桂卷我已经想着下周再来一个了。我点单的时候卡了一下，二十多种饮品一下子看不过来，犹豫了好一会儿，后面排队的人也有点急。要不试营业这段时间，先把招牌的六七款放在菜单最显眼的位置，其他的放到背面？我是真觉得这家店能做起来，才跟你说这些。
cases.note: 试营业正是能改的时候：只挑一个问题，说成自己点单时的感受，再给一个马上能试的办法。

cases.situation: My friend Marcus wants to quit his warehouse job in the spring and put his $20,000 savings into a taco truck. He had me over to taste the menu and asked for my honest opinion. The food was genuinely great, especially the birria, but when I asked how many tacos a day he'd need to sell to cover costs, he said he hadn't worked that out yet.
cases.reply: The birria was the standout for me, and the whole menu tasted like something people would queue for. The one thing I keep coming back to is the question from the other night: how many tacos a day you'd need to sell to cover costs. Before the $20,000 goes in, could you work that number out, maybe even test it with a few weekend pop-ups while you're still at the warehouse? I'm asking because I want this to work, not because I doubt the food.
cases.note: Specific praise for the food, then the missing break-even number as a question, because it is the one thing that protects his savings.

cases.situation: 表妹小雨10月10日周六要去纹身，把设计稿发给我问真实意见：手腕内侧一只小猫，尾巴绕成一个圈，下面是奶奶的名字“秀兰”。猫画得很可爱，但名字的字又细又小，我自己脚踝上那行小字三年后就有点糊了。
cases.reply: 小雨，稿子我仔细看了，小猫太可爱了，尾巴绕成一个圈那里特别有你的感觉。我唯一有点担心的是奶奶的名字：字这么细这么小，我脚踝上那行小字三年后就有点糊了。要不要跟纹身师商量一下，把“秀兰”放大一点、笔画加粗？离10号还有时间改，我是想让它十年后看着也跟现在一样好看。
cases.note: 纹身还没做，正是能改的时候：只提一个会随时间变坏的问题，用自己的经历来说，不评价她选的图案。

cases.situation: 表姐怀孕七个月，打算给女儿起名“林梓涵”，发微信问我真实意见。我很喜欢“涵”字，她说是希望孩子有涵养。但“梓涵”这几年特别常见，我女儿班上就有两个梓涵。
cases.reply: “涵”这个字选得真好，有涵养这个寓意我特别喜欢。你让我说真话，我就提一点：“梓涵”这几年挺多的，我女儿班上就有两个。要不保留“涵”，前面换个少见点的字？你们定什么我都喜欢，只是觉得这个名字值得独一无二。
cases.note: 只提一个问题，并用自己亲眼见到的例子说明；最后决定权明确交还给她。

cases.situation: 我妈退休后开始在短视频平台上发自己做家常菜的视频，已经发了十几条，让我说说真实意见。我最喜欢红烧肉那条，她边做边讲特别亲切。就是每条都有5分钟左右，开头差不多两分钟在聊买菜和家长里短，真正做菜要等好久。
cases.reply: 妈，你最近几条我都看完了，红烧肉那条我看着都饿了，你边做边讲的样子特别亲切，像在家里厨房听你说话。我就提一点：开头聊买菜那两分钟，我看的时候有点着急，想快点看你下锅。要不试试一开头先放做好的菜，然后直接开始做，聊天的话放到炖的时候说？你讲得这么好，我是想让更多人一直看到最后。
cases.note: 给长辈的意见也只提一个，用“我看的时候”说感受，再给一个马上能试的做法。

cases.situation: 大学同学阿泽想从销售转行做数据分析，把简历发我让我提真实意见，下周一开始投。他自学半年做了一个分析外卖平台评论的项目，写得很扎实，但放在第二页最底下，第一页全是以前做销售的经历。
cases.reply: 阿泽，简历我认真看了。外卖评论那个项目写得特别扎实，一看就是真下了半年功夫。我唯一的担心是它在第二页最底下，我是一路翻到最后才看到的，招聘的人可能看完第一页的销售经历就放下了。要不把这个项目挪到第一页最上面，销售经历压缩成几行？底子很好，调一下顺序，周一投出去会更有竞争力。
cases.note: 只提一个问题，用“我翻到最后才看到”说自己的阅读感受，再给一个周一前就能改好的办法。

cases.situation: My friend Jess drafted an email to her landlord about the mould in her bathroom and asked if it's okay to send tonight. The facts are strong: she reported it on 3 August and 1 September and attached photos. But the last paragraph calls him a slumlord and says she'll 'make sure everyone knows what he's like'.
cases.reply: The first part is really strong: two dates and photos, it's hard to argue with. The last paragraph is where I'd pause. I think 'slumlord' and 'make sure everyone knows' give him something to react to other than the mould. What if you ended with one clear ask instead, like the date by which you want someone to come and look at it? You're in the right here, which is exactly why I'd let the facts do the work.
cases.note: She asked 'okay to send?', so lead with what works and name the one change before she hits send.

cases.situation: Mi pareja, Andrés, va a hacer paella para mis padres el sábado 10 de octubre, la primera vez que cocina para ellos. Anoche hizo una prueba y hoy me escribe por WhatsApp desde el trabajo: '¿Qué te pareció de verdad?'. El socarrat le salió perfecto, pero el arroz estaba bastante salado.
cases.reply: ¿De verdad de verdad? El socarrat te salió perfecto, crujiente justo como tiene que ser. Lo único que noté es que el arroz me quedó un poco salado; quizá con menos sal en el caldo ya lo tienes. Si quieres, el jueves hacemos otra prueba juntos. Te lo digo porque el sábado te puede quedar buenísima.
cases.note: Un solo punto, concreto y fácil de arreglar, porque todavía hay tiempo antes del sábado.

cases.situation: My friend Sam's dad died last week and the funeral is Saturday. Sam asked me to read his eulogy draft and be honest; he has five minutes. The story about his dad waking him at 5am to fish at Lake Wren is beautiful, but most of the rest is a list of his dad's jobs and dates.
cases.reply: Sam, I read it twice. The story about your dad waking you at 5am to fish at Lake Wren is beautiful; that's him, I could see it. Where I lost him a little was the run of jobs and dates, which read more like a record than like your dad. What if you kept one line on his work and gave the rest of the five minutes to more moments like the lake? Whatever you decide, it's going to mean a lot to everyone there.
cases.note: Grief makes everything land harder: one point, framed as your experience as a reader, and if he sounds raw, say it on a call rather than by text.

cases.situation: My grandma Joan, 84, asked me on the phone why hardly anyone in the family replies to her emails. They're full of lovely news, like last week's one about the robins nesting in her porch light, but she writes everything in capital letters, and my younger cousins read that as shouting. I'm visiting her on Sunday and want to text her before then.
cases.reply: Gran, I love your emails; the one about the robins nesting in your porch light made my week. Since you asked, I think I know one reason the cousins go quiet: everything's in capital letters, and they read that as shouting, even though I know you're not. It's an easy fix, and I can show you how on Sunday. Your news is too good to go unanswered.
cases.note: She asked, so give the one real reason as how others read it, not a verdict on her, and make the fix something you do together.

cases.situation: 好朋友周周明天下午去一家律所面试行政岗，发来穿搭照片问我真实意见。米色西装外套很合身，但里面配的是一件印着大卡通图案的T恤。她衣柜里有件白衬衫，上次见她穿过。
cases.reply: 外套选得特别好，很合身，整个人看着很利落。我唯一会换的是里面那件卡通T恤，律所的面试官可能会先注意到图案，而不是你。换上你那件白衬衫会不会更稳？你本来就很适合这个岗位，我是想让人第一眼就看到这一点。
cases.note: 面试前一天还来得及改：只提一处，给一个她衣柜里现成的替换，不评价她的身材或品味。

cases.situation: My friend Callum spent three years writing his first fantasy novel and plans to send it to literary agents next month. He asked me to be brutally honest. The world-building is wonderful, especially the floating salt markets, but his hero Wren doesn't make a single choice of her own until chapter 6; things just happen to her.
cases.reply: You asked me to be straight, so I will be: I don't think it's ready for agents yet, and I think it's close. The floating salt markets are some of the best world-building I've read. What held me back is Wren. She doesn't make a choice of her own until chapter 6, so for the first five chapters I was watching things happen to her rather than following her. If she made one real decision in chapter 1, I think the whole opening would come alive. I'd rather you hear it from me now than get a form rejection that tells you nothing.
cases.note: When they ask for brutal and it isn't ready, say so plainly once, then give the one fix that matters most.

cases.situation: Meu irmão Rafael está aprendendo a pintar retratos a óleo e me pediu uma opinião sincera sobre o retrato da nossa avó, que ele quer dar no aniversário de 90 anos dela, dia 18 de outubro. Os olhos ficaram idênticos, com aquele jeito dela quando ri, mas a pele ficou acinzentada e ela parece doente.
cases.reply: Rafa, os olhos ficaram idênticos, é o olhar da vó quando ela ri de alguma coisa. O que me pegou foi a pele: para mim ficou meio acinzentada, e ela parece cansada, quase doente. Será que um tom mais quente no rosto resolveria? Falo isso porque acho que esse quadro vai ser o presente que ela mais vai guardar.
cases.note: Uma única observação, descrita como impressão sua, sobre algo que ele ainda pode mudar antes do dia 18.

cases.situation: 我在一个网上写作小组里，组员“青柠”发了一篇八千字的短篇小说求真实点评，写一个女孩在县城陪外婆度过的最后一个夏天。外婆教她腌梅子那段写得特别好，但结尾突然揭晓“原来一切都是梦”，我读完有点失落。我们素不相识。
cases.reply: 谢谢分享，我认真读完了。外婆教她腌梅子那段特别好，我读的时候好像真的坐在那个院子里。我读完有点失落的是结尾：揭晓“一切都是梦”之后，前面那个夏天在我心里一下子变轻了。如果结尾留在真实的夏天里，会不会更有力量？只是一个读者的感受，供你参考，这篇真的值得改好。
cases.note: 对陌生人的作品也只提一个问题，用“我读完的感受”来讲，不评价作者本人，最后把决定权留给她。

cases.situation: My friend Leo has started a podcast interviewing local small-business owners and sent me episode 3, with the woman who runs the bike repair shop, asking what I really think before he records episode 4 on Saturday. His questions are well researched and the one about her first year nearly going bust was great, but he cuts in on her answers a lot, five or six times in the first ten minutes alone, and I kept losing her thread.
cases.reply: Listened to the whole thing. Your questions are clearly well researched, and the one about her first year nearly going bust was the best moment; I was hooked. The one thing I noticed was that you cut in on her answers quite a lot, five or six times in the first ten minutes, and I kept losing her thread. For Saturday, maybe try counting two seconds after she stops before you come in? I'm only saying it because your questions are good enough that the answers deserve the room.
cases.note: One habit he can change before the next recording, described as a listener's experience, not a verdict on him as a host.
